Application Materials.content:
- Mandatory for all applicants: **Academic transcripts**.
- Course-specific requirements may include samples of written work or professional portfolio work, personal statement, curriculum vitae (CV) or resume, and academic reference ([Guidance for references (PDF, 54kb)](https://www.york.ac.uk/media/study-new/postgraduate/postgraduatetaught/applying/guidance-for-references.pdf)).
- International applicants: Evidence of your English language ability.
- A transcript must be provided with your application before it's submitted. If you've completed your studies, provide copies of your degree certificates and formal transcripts of your academic record, including full details of degrees, classifications, grades obtained and modules/units taken. If the qualification was taken in a non-English-speaking country, provide documents in the original language with a formally certified English translation. If you have not yet finished your studies, provide an interim transcript of results to date.
- Written work: some courses require a sample of written work; details of what is required will be in the application form. [Find out more about course-specific written work requirements](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/documents/written-work/).
- Personal statement: a personal statement can be included as part of your application; for some courses it forms part of the assessment process. Details of what to include will be provided during the application process. [Find out more about course-specific requirements for personal statements](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/documents/personal-statements/).
- Curriculum vitae/resume: your CV or resume can be uploaded as part of your application to provide further information on prior experience and qualifications.
- Academic referee: you will need to supply the details of **one referee** when you submit your application. The referee may be contacted by email and asked to provide a reference if needed. You should provide an academic referee if you have graduated within the last five years.
- If English is not your first language, you may be asked to provide evidence of your English language ability to the required level. If you've taken an [approved English language test](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/international/english/), upload a copy of your certificate.
- File formats: Word (.doc or .docx), Acrobat (.pdf), text (.txt); scanned documents should be JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg), Acrobat (.pdf) or GIF (.gif). **Each document must be less than 1MB**.
- Multiple page documents, such as a transcript, should be scanned as **one file**, eg a single PDF, and should not fill more than one document slot.
- Additional documents can be provided after submitting your application via your You@York account. Do not email documents because this will cause delays in assessing your application.

Application Deadlines.content:
If you're an international student, it's best to apply by **early June** to avoid any issues with accommodation or visa applications.
Applications to study a postgraduate taught course at York in 2026/27 close on **28 August 2026** for international applications (excluding online courses). Some courses may have earlier closing dates.

Academic Requirements.content:
| Qualification | Typical offer |
| --- | --- |
| Undergraduate degree | **A 2:2 or equivalent in an undergraduate degree in any subject**, provided that previous studies have included **computer programming and quantitative methods such as calculus, linear algebra, probability, and statistics**. |
| Other international qualifications | [Equivalent qualifications from your country](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/international/your-country/) |
For applicants from China applying to postgraduate taught courses: you would normally need a Bachelors degree from a recognised institution in a relevant subject. The score needed depends on which university you attended in China and which subject you are applying to. Typically you'll need at least the equivalent of a UK lower second class honours degree (2:2). Actual requirements will vary by course. **A score of 75 to 80% is considered comparable to a UK 2:1; a score of 70 to 75% is considered comparable to a UK 2:2**.

The length of course you need to take depends on your current English language test scores and how much you need to improve to reach the English language requirements. After you've accepted your offer to study at York, they'll confirm which pre-sessional course you should apply to via [You@York](https://www.york.ac.uk/you-at-york/).

Program Overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics starts in September 2026 and is a **1 year full-time** course in the [School for Business and Society](https://www.york.ac.uk/business-society/). It is designed to develop competent analytics professionals using artificial intelligence, statistics and operational research to tackle complex business and societal challenges.
The MSc provides an in-depth understanding of data science principles and analytics techniques. Taught by leading analytics researchers and practitioners, it equips students with essential skills in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, operational research, computer programming, and their applications within business and society. The programme emphasises social responsibility and environmental sustainability, preparing students to address real-world challenges effectively and ethically.
Python is used as the main programming language for essential data science and analytics modules, including computer programming, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, operational research, and data communication. The course covers the business analytics life cycle, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. Alongside the core curriculum, students choose option modules across business and management, social science, science, and engineering disciplines, allowing them to customise their studies around advanced data science and analytics methods and business or societal applications. The course also develops independent research skills leading to an applied-focus dissertation project.
The course is taught through a combination of lectures and practical workshops, with most modules featuring more workshops than lectures. Teaching focuses heavily on practical data science and business analytics skills using Python for real-world application. Each module consists of 20 credits, with the final research task totalling 60 credits. Assessment includes computer programmes, written reports, oral presentations and a poster.
Students are based in the [School for Business and Society](https://www.york.ac.uk/map/#locid271) on Campus West. Most teaching takes place in the Church Lane Building, with additional contact hours elsewhere on Campus East and Campus West. The Church Lane Building features modern teaching rooms, a café, and spaces for group work and socialising. The programme also uses well-equipped computer classrooms with software available on Windows, Mac and Linux-based operating systems.
The School for Business and Society is a UK top 30 research department for management according to the Times Higher Education ranking of the latest REF results (2021). The programme is taught by world-leading academics in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, business analytics, and operational research, and the faculty includes authors of world-leading textbooks taught on the programme.
Career preparation includes opportunities to apply knowledge through complex real-world problems, case studies, group projects, and an applied dissertation. Career opportunities listed for graduates include business analyst, market research analyst, quantitative analyst, policy analyst, data scientist, analytics engineer, and management consultant. Transferable skills include data science and analytics techniques, artificial intelligence and machine learning knowledge, statistical analysis, operational research and data visualisation, critical thinking and problem solving, data communication and presentation skills, project management and leadership skills, and research capabilities.

Curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Length: **1 year full-time**.
Course content: Python is used as the main programming language for the essential data science and analytics modules, including computer programming, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, operational research, and data communication. The modules aim to give a thorough understanding of the business analytics life cycle, covering descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. Alongside the core curriculum, students choose option modules across business and management, social science, science, and engineering disciplines. Independent research skills lead to an applied-focus dissertation project.
Core modules:
- [**Programming for Data Science**](https://www.york.ac.uk/students/studying/manage/programmes/module-catalogue/module/CHE00044M/latest)

Each module consists of **20 credits**, with the final research task totalling **60 credits**. The course is taught as a combination of lectures and practical workshops, with most modules featuring more workshops than lectures. Teaching is heavily focused on practical data science and business analytics skills with Python. Students are based in the [School for Business and Society](https://www.york.ac.uk/map/#locid271) on Campus West; most teaching takes place in the Church Lane Building, with additional contact hours elsewhere on Campus East and Campus West.

For 2026/27 postgraduate students, the fixed living/study/travel cost of attendance for a **1st year student on a one-year course** is **£25,663 + tuition**; extracting only the non-tuition portion, the cost of attendance is **£25,663**. The example is based on “a 1st year student on a one-year course living in on-campus accommodation.”
| Expenditure | Weekly cost | Annual cost (51 weeks) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Food | £54 | £2,754 |
| Toiletries | £22 | £1,122 |
| Course related costs | | £1,275 |

| Laundry | £11.20 | £571 |
| Social and sporting activities | £40 | £1,913 |

| Mid-range ensuite campus accommodation | £212 | £10,812 |

Multiple Applications.content: You can only accept one unconditional offer with us. If we make you an offer for more than one course, you will need to decide which one to accept.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: You can apply to defer entry before enrolment from your [You@York account](https://www.york.ac.uk/you-at-york/), or by emailing [pg-admissions@york.ac.uk](mailto:pg-admissions@york.ac.uk). Applications are considered on an individual basis and must be made before **16 October 2026** (for the 2026/27 cycle).

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
There are two types of offer that you might receive.
- **Conditional offers**: York makes conditional offers when there are criteria you need to meet before you can start your course. If your offer is conditional, the conditions of entry will be included in your offer letter.
- Offer conditions typically fall into three categories: **academic**, **language** (if you're a non-native English-speaking applicant you must provide evidence of your English language proficiency), and **reference conditions**.
- Supporting documents needed to meet the conditions of your offer should be uploaded via You@York. If you do not meet the original conditions of your offer, you should upload your documentation anyway, as York may be able to reconsider you.
- Once you have met all the conditions of your offer, York will email you confirming this, and an unconditional offer letter will be available online to download and print.
- If you require a Student Visa, York can issue your CAS once your offer becomes unconditional, and not longer than six months before your course starts.
